$comment: Domain-rule invariants — the half of the oracle set that CANNOT be derived from CRUD shape. The generative oracle emits I1-I11 from a surface's metamodel; those catch structural bugs blind. These are different: business rules that no shape analysis can infer, harvested from documented sources per PLAN_FORCED_DISCOVERY_LOCATOR_EXHAUSTION 'Domain-rule harvest'.
harvestedBy: CEO (Jira read-only via Atlassian MCP, cloudId 03ec286f-d928-4c2c-b782-c8cce703ce2a) + repo-documented rules
provenanceRule: Every invariant carries a source a human can open. An invariant with no openable source is not a domain rule, it is an assumption — do not add one.

coverage.honestNote: A JQL sweep of 110 recent NAV issues surfaced exactly ONE rule-bearing summary (NAV-4529). Domain rules in this tracker live in issue DESCRIPTIONS and acceptance criteria, not summaries, so summary-level search systematically under-returns. A complete harvest needs a description-level pass over the NAV project plus the Confluence spec space — a dedicated research session. Treat this as a working seed with real rows, NOT the finished corpus.

coverageGaps: permission-invariant (D20): the kernel oracles and generated invariants I1-I11 all reason about a single actor's view. None re-executes an action under a DIFFERENT ROLE and asserts refusal. A read-only-role bypass is therefore invisible to every oracle currently implemented, and to any walk performed as an admin. Closing this needs a role-partition oracle, which does not exist yet.

invariants.rule: A Priceguide list must save and remain visible for a location whose only currency is non-USD (e.g. a CAD-only Canadian location).
invariants.observedViolation: After save the list appears empty.
invariants.censusNote: Status is Done but the defect text describes live behaviour — the NM-2011 class (Jira status contradicting live behaviour). Verify against the live surface before this status steers any disposition.

invariants.rule: The Print button must be disabled when the Priceguide list did not persist. An enabled Print control asserts that a save succeeded.
invariants.observedViolation: Print stays enabled after a failed save; printing yields 'An error occured while loading the report.'
invariants.whyItMatters: A control whose ENABLED state is itself a claim about persisted state. A walk that only checks 'is the button clickable' records a pass while the save failed — the NM-2186 shape, found in the wild on a different surface.

invariants.rule: The generated report must render prices in the currency selected on the parameter screen.
invariants.observedViolation: Report prints USD regardless of the currency selected (MXN/CAD).
invariants.whyItMatters: A selector that changes nothing — the 1222 dead-filter shape. A walk toggling currency and seeing prices unchanged must reach DIFFERENTIAL-DATA-REQUIRED, not 'toggled, no change, fine'.

invariants.rule: The currency selector must offer only currencies configured for that location.
invariants.observedViolation: A CAD-only location still offers USD.

invariants.rule: Report generation must succeed for a location that does not support USD.
The UI must indicate which currency it is displaying for international locations (MXN, CAD).
Labor product groups populate only on the master corporate office (1101). An empty Labor surface on another office is a DATA STATE, not a defect and not 'covered'.
invariants.source: CLAUDE.md — LR-ENC-005 (office 1101 is the master/superset corporate location); NM-1881
invariants.whyItMatters: The 2026-06-19 M4 miss: an empty Labor override tab accepted as 'empty / refresh later' and closed. The population path existed; nobody looked for it.

invariants.rule: The override picker is currency-gated; an empty picker on a non-matching-currency location is expected behaviour, not a defect.
invariants.sourceDetail: NM-2076 — 'Pricing Override – Product Group not displayed and Currency field disabled for Canada and some Mexico locations'. Confirms the gating is real and country-linked, not a data-state artefact.

invariants.rule: Product Group 286 may not carry a blank Override Price.
invariants.verificationNote: Two independent Jira searches (`text ~ 286 AND text ~ override`, and `blank override price` / `override price required` / `product group 286`) returned NO governing ticket. The rule appears only in this repo's own plan body, so it may be a walk observation that was promoted to a 'rule' without a source. **Do not let this steer a disposition until a source is found** — an unsourced rule is exactly the claim-without-census that oracle 5 exists to catch. Retained rather than deleted so the gap stays visible.

invariants.surface: Pricing Setup > Pricing Details AND Corporate Pricing > Product Group Override
invariants.rule: A Max Discount Percent value under 1% must persist exactly as entered. Clicking out of the field and back in must not shift the decimal or inflate the stored value, and the two pages must parse percentages identically.
invariants.observedViolation: `.003` reloads as 30% — the decimal shifts two places, turning 0.3% into 30%, with NO validation error shown. Reproduces on both pages.
invariants.whyItMatters: A 100x error on a discount field, applied silently. This is write-then-read-back — the system's own output not surviving its own input, at field level rather than file level. A walk that types a value and sees it accepted records a pass; the corruption only appears on re-entry.

invariants.rule: Special rate must always be permitted for Digital Branding.
invariants.harvestNote: Rule taken from the issue summary; the description was not read in this pass. Confirm the exact conditions before this steers a disposition.

invariants.rule: Canada only — Venue Price Book is configured as the default for Production Orders.
invariants.harvestNote: Country-gated default. Same summary-only caveat as D11.

invariants.rule: The Corp Price Override screen must remain viewable after a new price strategy assignment.
invariants.observedViolation: Screen not viewable after a new price strategy assignment when the new PB/PS was involved.

invariants.rule: A file produced by the system's own Export must be accepted by its own Import.
invariants.observedViolation: A valid exported file fails on import with 'Invalid Line / Required Fields Missing'.
invariants.whyItMatters: This is the canonical round-trip bug the parent plan cites by number; it now carries its real Jira source. Oracle 3 exists because of this ticket.

invariants.rule: A sort must order the FULL result set, not just the rows on the current page.
invariants.observedViolation: Search sort applies to the current page only.
invariants.whyItMatters: A page-scoped sort looks correct on screen and is wrong in the data — the same read-what-is-rendered mistake as counting DOM nodes on a virtualized grid.

invariants.rule: Changing the sort must order across the whole import set, not only within a single Product Group ID.

invariants.surface: Corporate Pricing > Import Max Discount > Publish
invariants.rule: The Publish screen must show every record in the import, and the set must be stable between views.
invariants.observedViolation: Only some records show, and the subset changes on each view.
invariants.whyItMatters: A non-deterministic record set is the worst case for a count oracle — two honest observations disagree, so any single reading is unsafe.

invariants.rule: The Barcodeable checkbox must be read-only when on the Item segment.
Save/Update enablement must track actual form validity — the control must not remain disabled after the user makes the form valid, nor become disabled on a legitimate edit.
invariants.observedViolation: Save becomes disabled after adding a location with an existing entry (NM-3063); Update stays disabled after toggling Implied Discount (NM-2917).
invariants.whyItMatters: Same family as D2: a control's enabled state is a CLAIM about system state. A walk that reads enablement as truth records a pass while the form is in the opposite condition.

invariants.rule: A user holding a read-only role for a location must not be able to mutate that location's data. Read-only must be enforced server-side, not merely by hiding controls.
invariants.observedViolation: A user with the Sales Read Only role for a location IS able to add recommendations to the Price Guide.
invariants.whyItMatters: No oracle in the current set catches this. The 5 kernel oracles and the generated I1-I11 all reason about a single actor's view of data; none re-runs an action under a different ROLE and asserts it is refused. A walk performed as an admin cannot observe this defect at all — the control is present and works. This is a genuine coverage gap in the oracle set, not just a missing row.

invariants.rule: Proposal creation must be prevented while an active or pending Quote DocuSign exists.
An order carrying an implied-only discount must still trigger approval when approval is required.
invariants.observedViolation: Some orders with implied-only discount do not trigger approval although approval is needed.
invariants.whyItMatters: A gate that silently does not fire — the 1222 dead-control shape applied to an approval workflow rather than a filter.

invariants.rule: Location Settings must save when only the first-column fields are updated on a new or blank location.
invariants.observedViolation: Save is not possible in that state.

invariants.rule: When updating, the user must be able to select a single Tax Type or multiple Tax Types — but not all.
ODDB enable/disable is country-gated; today only US carries the flag.
invariants.whyItMatters: Same family as D8/D12: a surface that is legitimately empty or disabled for one country and a defect for another. Without the census, a walk on a non-US location reads the disabled state as a bug, or reads it as fine, with equal confidence.

invariants.rule: Each Product Group Override record is stored as one document per LocationNo with nested Currencies[].Overrides[]. Each override entry carries Price, MaxAllowedDiscount, and an Active flag. The export resolves the current corp price from the location's default corp strategies via cache.
invariants.provenanceNote: Design spec for the Pricing Microservice rewrite — describes intended storage shape, not observed live behaviour. Author: Akash Dubey; last modified Jul 02 2026.

invariants.rule: There are two distinct MaxAllowedDiscount levels: pricebook level (ProductGroupPricing.MaxAllowedDiscount) and override level (ProductGroupOverrideDetail.MaxAllowedDiscount). Export supports a max-discount mode that emits discount columns instead of prices.
invariants.provenanceNote: Design spec for the Pricing Microservice rewrite — describes intended discount model, not observed live behaviour. Author: Akash Dubey; last modified Jul 02 2026.
invariants.whyItMatters: A walk that tests MaxAllowedDiscount at only one level may miss a bug where the pricebook-level cap is not honoured by the override-level value, or vice versa. The export mode difference means export tests must cover both price-column and discount-column outputs.

invariants.rule: All Product Group Override endpoints require authentication under Azure B2C. GET endpoints are gated by the PricingRead policy; POST and non-strategy DELETE endpoints by PricingWrite; DELETE for a pricing strategy by PricingDelete. Audit username is captured on writes via IIdentityProvider.GetUsername().
invariants.provenanceNote: Design spec for the Pricing Microservice rewrite — describes intended authorization policies, not observed live enforcement. Author: Akash Dubey; last modified Jul 02 2026.
invariants.whyItMatters: The read/write/delete policy split cannot be derived from CRUD shape alone. A role-partition oracle must assert both directions: a PricingRead-only credential must be refused by mutating endpoints. These are the exact policy names the service enforces per the design spec.
